prompt:
﻿# genui_gen_v4_compact

You are a GenUICraft generator.
Convert the RESPONSE text into valid GenUICraft v0.9 server-to-client messages.

RESPONSE:
Assumptions:
- The trek is 10 days on the trail, not including travel days to/from Kathmandu/Lukla.
- A porter will carry your main luggage (duffel bag), so a smaller daypack is also needed for daily essentials.
- You will be staying in teahouses, so a tent and cooking equipment are not required.
- Temperatures range from 15°C during the day at lower altitudes to -10°C or colder at night and higher altitudes.

Everest Base Camp Trek Packing List (October)

Icons:
- Clothing: https://example.com/clothing_icon.png
- Gear: https://example.com/gear_icon.png
- Hygiene & Personal Care: https://example.com/hygiene_icon.png
- First-Aid & Health: https://example.com/first_aid_icon.png

Clothing:
- Base Layers (2-3 sets):
  - Lightweight, moisture-wicking thermal tops and bottoms (merino wool or synthetic).
- Mid Layers (2-3 items):
  - Fleece jacket (200-300 weight).
  - Light down jacket or synthetic insulated jacket.
- Outer Layers (1-2 items):
  - Waterproof and windproof shell jacket (Gore-Tex or similar).
  - Warm down jacket (600-800 fill power) for evenings and higher altitudes.
- Trekking Pants (2 pairs):
  - Durable, quick-drying trekking trousers (convertible options are good).
  - Fleece-lined or warm trekking pants for colder days.
- Warm Trousers/Fleece Pants (1 pair):
  - For evenings at teahouses.
- Underwear (5-7 pairs):
  - Moisture-wicking, comfortable.
- Socks (5-6 pairs):
  - Wool or synthetic trekking socks (various thicknesses).
  - Liner socks (optional, helps prevent blisters).
- Gloves (2 pairs):
  - Thin liner gloves.
  - Warm, waterproof outer gloves or mittens.
- Headwear (2-3 items):
  - Warm wool or fleece beanie/hat.
  - Sun hat or cap.
  - Neck gaiter or buff.
- Sleepwear:
  - Can use a clean set of base layers.

Gear:
- Backpacks:
  - Large duffel bag (80-100L) for porter (often provided by trekking agency, confirm).
  - Daypack (25-35L) for personal daily essentials (water, snacks, camera, layers).
- Sleeping Bag:
  - Rated to at least -10°C (comfort rating), possibly -15°C to -20°C for colder sleepers.
- Footwear:
  - Sturdy, waterproof, broken-in trekking boots (mid to high-ankle support).
  - Camp shoes, sandals, or crocs for evenings in teahouses.
- Trekking Poles:
  - Highly recommended for stability and reducing knee strain.
- Water Storage:
  - 2 x 1L Nalgene bottles (can be filled with hot water for warmth at night).
  - Hydration reservoir (2-3L, ensure tube doesn't freeze at high altitude).
- Headlamp:
  - With fresh batteries and spare set.
- Eyewear:
  - High-quality sunglasses with UV protection (Category 3 or 4).
- Electronics:
  - Power bank/portable charger.
  - Camera, extra batteries, memory cards.
  - Phone and charger.
  - Universal travel adapter (Nepal uses Type C, D, and M sockets).
- Miscellaneous:
  - Quick-dry towel.
  - Small padlock for duffel bag.
  - Dry bags or plastic bags for organizing clothes and electronics.
  - Book, journal, pen.
  - Trekking map (optional, often provided by guide).
  - Small thermos (optional, for hot drinks).
  - Snacks (energy bars, dried fruit, nuts, chocolate - personal preference).
  - Reusable shopping bag (for souvenirs).

Hygiene & Personal Care:
- Toiletries:
  - Toothbrush, toothpaste.
  - Biodegradable soap/shampoo (small travel sizes).
  - Deodorant.
  - Small mirror (optional).
- Hand Sanitizer:
  - Essential for hygiene on the trail.
- Wet Wipes:
  - For sponge baths or cleaning.
- Sun Protection:
  - High SPF sunscreen (SPF 30-50+).
  - Lip balm with SPF.
- Toilet Paper:
  - Small roll, as not always available in teahouse toilets.
- Moisturizer:
  - For face and hands, to combat dry air.
- Personal Medications:
  - Any prescription medications you require (with a copy of the prescription).
- Feminine Hygiene Products:
  - As needed.

First-Aid & Health:
- Basic Pain Relief:
  - Ibuprofen,

Output contract:
- Output ONLY a JSON array (no markdown, no prose).
- Each array item must be one v0.9 message object.
- Allowed message types only: `createSurface`, `updateComponents`, `updateDataModel`, `deleteSurface`.
- Add `createSurface` before any updates.
- `createSurface.catalogId` must be `https://genui.local/specification/v0_9/standard_catalog.json`.
- Include exactly one `updateComponents` message with a complete component set.
- In that set, include exactly one component with `id: "root"` as tree root.
- Component ids must be unique; all child references must resolve.
- Use only catalog-supported components and properties.

Component guidance:
- Prefer structured UI over text dumps.
- Use `Card`, `Row`, `Column`, `List`, `Tabs`, `Divider`, `Button` where appropriate.
- Convert action-like links/"Quick Actions" to `Button` with `action.functionCall.call = "openUrl"`.
- Preserve key content (assumptions, options, comparisons, totals, sources) without hallucination.
- If dynamic rows are useful, use `updateDataModel` + template children binding.

Assets and URLs:
- For media, use only local asset paths that start with `/`.
- Never output remote image/icon URLs.
- For web actions, `openUrl` targets may be remote URLs.

Validation reminders:
- `version` must be `"v0.9"` on every message.
- `updateComponents.components` must be a non-empty array.
- Keep JSON strictly valid.
